messages:
kevin: Heads-up — our canary gate accepted an operator override earlier but the deploy proceeded without an audit entry for the approval. Suspect stale KMS token validation during the gate check.

maya: Wait, operator override? which service? link the rollout? :eyes:

kevin: rollout/id=service-recommendations-canary-2026-03, triggered ~10:42 UTC. infra-bot posted the canary state change: 'canary_approved_by=jamie'. No matching audit log from auditsvc for that approval.

jamie: I clicked approve in the console at 10:41:58. I got a quick spinner then green. Didn’t see an error.

lena: if KMS signing failed, the UI could have shown success but we might have skipped server-side verification. Need logs from gate service and KMS client.

kevin: can someone grep the gate logs for the approval request id? I think it’s in the rollout object: `approval_ref: 0x7a9f21`

jamie: running `kubectl -n infra logs deploy/gatekeeper -c gate | grep 7a9f21` now

infra-bot: deploy/gatekeeper restarted at 2026-03-12T10:42:05Z due to OOM kill (node pool surge).

maya: OOM restart could have dropped in-flight KMS cache or background signer queue. Maybe the gate validated the cached signature locally without hitting auditsvc. We should check whether the gate treats a locally cached token as authoritative.

kevin: auditsvc logs show no entry for `approval_ref: 0x7a9f21`. snippet I pulled: ```[2026-03-12T10:41:58Z] auditsvc: no entry found for approval_ref=0x7a9f21 on service-recommendations-canary```

lena: that implies a missing remote write. Check KMS client errors in gate logs — maybe it failed to sign the approval and gate fell back to previous signed token.

jamie: gate logs show `WARN KMS client: token expired, falling back to cached-sig` at 10:41:57. Then immediately `INFO Approval accepted by operator jamie`, with no downstream publish attempt recorded.

maya: mitigation: pause the canary rollout and revoke the applied change. Can we trigger an automatic rollback? We have a canary fallback policy but it relies on proper audit state.

kevin: immediate steps I suggest: 1) Pause new canaries via admin toggle (I can flip now). 2) Revoke any pending operator overrides in the gate DB. 3) Force auditsvc to rescan recent approvals and reconcile. 4) Patch gate to treat cached-sig as insufficient unless auditsvc acknowledged the write.

jamie: Agree. Also, rotate KMS client token on gate nodes to avoid stale caches. I'll push a token refresh and restart gate pods gracefully.

lena: for short-term: set gate to fail-closed (deny) on approval signature mismatch. Long-term: require synchronous acknowledgement from auditsvc before marking approved.

kevin: who's owning the post-incident triage? we need a short blameless writeup for compliance. Also need to check if any A/B test exposures used this path.

maya: I'll own the triage doc. I'll collect: timeline, affected rollouts, KMS error metrics, gate pod OOM history, and audit gaps.

auditsvc: automated note: reconciler job queued for window 2026-03-12T10:30Z-10:45Z. Will attempt to rehydrate missing approval records and emit findings to #eng-security (ETA ~15m).

kevin: thanks. After mitigations, we should add an e2e test that simulates KMS client failures and verifies we never accept cached approvals without audit confirmation.

jamie: adding test story to platform sprint. Also creating a temporary alert: `gate.approval.missing_audit` if approval accepted but auditsvc has no record after 30s.

maya: deployed pause flag and revoked pending overrides. kms token rotation started. auditsvc reconciliation in progress.

kevin: OK closing loop here — once auditsvc posts findings, we’ll reconvene for RCA and next-actions. Good catch, team. :thumbsup:
